 Police investigate former Prince Andrew's time with Jeffrey Epstein, Ghislaine Maxwell at Balmoral 
 "The needs of victim survivors at the heart of those enquiries," police said. 
 13:34 Britain's Prince Andrew, Duke of York leaves after attending the Easter Matins service at St George's Chapel at Windsor Castle, in Windsor on April 20, 2025. Scottish police are in the "very early stage" of probing late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell's reported 1999 stay at the royal Balmoral estate at the invite of ex-prince Andrew, UK media reported Friday, October 30, 2026. Kirsty Wigglesworth/POOL/AFP via Getty Images By Jon Haworth and Katie Kindelan October 30, 2026, 2:14 PM Share Follow ABC News on Google -- Authorities in Scotland are investigating information about time spent by Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor , Ghislaine Maxwell and Jeffrey Epstein at Balmoral, the royal family's private estate in Scotland.
 A Police Scotland spokesperson told ABC News in a statement Friday the investigation is "at a very early stage."
 “We have received information and active enquiries are ongoing but these are at a very early stage,” the spokesperson said. “All enquiries are evidence led, with the needs of victim survivors at the heart of those enquiries. We would never confirm details of ongoing enquiries and it would be inappropriate to comment further.”
 Britain's Prince Andrew, Duke of York leaves after attending the Easter Matins service at St George's Chapel at Windsor Castle, in Windsor on April 20, 2025. Scottish police are in the "very early stage" of probing late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell's reported 1999 stay at the royal Balmoral estate at the invite of ex-prince Andrew, UK media reported Friday, October 30, 2026. Kirsty Wigglesworth/POOL/AFP via Getty Images Police Scotland did not name Mountbatten-Windsor, Epstein or Maxwell in its statement. The force provided the statement in response to a direct request for comment about their time at Balmoral.
 Maxwell is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence in the U.S. following her 2021 conviction on five felony counts arising from her participation with Epstein in the sexual abuse of young girls over the course of a decade.  
 Related Ghislaine Maxwell's family says she will continue to fight charges she aided Epstein Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly known as Prince Andrew, has previously denied wrongdoing with respect to Epstein, who died by suicide in 2019 while awaiting trial on charges of sex trafficking minor girls.

 Two years ago, Mountbatten-Windsor -- a brother of King Charles III -- was stripped of his “prince” title and later moved out of his royal residence amid fallout from his interactions with Epstein.
 In February, the former prince was   arrested   on suspicion of misconduct in public office stemming from his time as a U.K. trade envoy, a role in which he was responsible for promoting British business interests abroad.
 Related Man arrested near former Prince Andrew's home appears in court The allegations against Mountbatten-Windsor came after his name appeared in the 3 million pages of documents related to Epstein released by the U.S. Department of Justice in January.
 Mountbatten-Windsor was released under investigation on the evening of his arrest and was not charged.
 Buckingham Palace told ABC News Friday the palace does not speak for Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, and cannot comment on an ongoing police investigation.
